decisions.decision: Preserve true CLI, filesystem, data, and external-system seams; remove internal validation or adapters only after callers and tests prove them redundant.
decisions.evidence: The requested cleanup spans tools, data artifacts, workflow hooks, and trading code with distinct system seams.

entries.name: principle-build-the-lever
entries.reason: The plan will specify a cleanup manifest and verifier, but building those implementation artifacts now would violate plan-flow.

decisions.decision: Replace repeated operational prose with discoverable config, generated indexes, or checks; retain judgment-heavy decisions in one durable source.
decisions.evidence: START_HERE.md repeats commands and workflow policy that also exist in scripts, hooks, and AGENTS.md.

decisions.decision: Compare at least three target repository shapes before selecting the phased migration.
decisions.evidence: The whole-repository restructure has no single obvious file layout and plan-flow requires alternatives.

decisions.decision: Optimize the entry path for the next agent and maintainer so START_HERE.md answers where to begin without caching discoverable facts.
decisions.evidence: The user explicitly named START_HERE.md as the universal entry point.

entries.name: principle-fix-root-causes
entries.reason: No defect is being debugged; obsolete-file judgments will use dependency and history evidence instead.

decisions.decision: Define the file-liveness classification and target information hierarchy before planning moves or deletions.
decisions.evidence: Lossless cleanup depends on distinguishing authoritative, generated, reproducible, historical, and dead material.

decisions.decision: Partition exploration by code, documentation, and data or operations, and retain only file pointers and findings in the main thread.
decisions.evidence: The repository has enough files and long documents to overwhelm one undifferentiated scan.

decisions.decision: Prefer deletion, consolidation, and flatter ownership over new layers or replacement documentation.
decisions.evidence: The user's desired end state is an extremely lean repository with no functionality loss.

decisions.decision: Require the eventual inventory, move, archive, and delete operations to be dry-runnable and safe after partial completion.
decisions.evidence: A whole-repository cleanup can be interrupted and must converge without duplicating or losing files.

decisions.decision: Move imports, command references, documentation pointers, and tests in the same phase that removes each old path.
decisions.evidence: The user wants the old code gone, and internal callers do not justify compatibility layers.

decisions.decision: Measure cleanup candidates by layers to trace and hidden state to remember, then collapse one-caller wrappers and duplicate knowledge.
decisions.evidence: START_HERE.md currently asks a newcomer to cross several documents and retain historical state before acting.

decisions.decision: Represent the audit as a file-liveness registry with ownership, authority, reproducibility, consumers, replacement, and disposition fields.
decisions.evidence: Scattered keep or delete judgments would otherwise repeat shape assumptions across hundreds of files.

decisions.decision: Infer reversible planning choices from repository evidence and surface any real product decision in the completed plan instead of pausing the audit.
decisions.evidence: The user supplied the target, exclusions, and lossless constraint; the remaining work is observable.

decisions.decision: Plan explicit verification points that converge on the target tree without permanent redirect files or dual documentation systems.
decisions.evidence: The requested end state is one clear entry path and a lean tree, not a long compatibility period.

decisions.decision: Every proposed deletion class needs direct proof from imports, invocations, tests, artifacts, or reproducibility before removal; the final tree needs full checks and smoke runs.
decisions.evidence: The user made losslessness the acceptance condition.

decisions.decision: Design the target repository as if START_HERE.md, durable memory, and the live trading workflow had been foundational, then migrate toward it in checked phases.
decisions.evidence: The user requested an entire repository restructure rather than local tidying.

entries.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
entries.reason: Explorers are read-only and the implementation plan will sequence repository writes; no concurrent mutable target is required.

decisions.decision: Split the cleanup into inventory, retirement, code consolidation, layout migration, documentation compression, and final proof units, each ending in checks.
decisions.evidence: A repository-wide migration cannot be verified honestly as one batch.

decisions.decision: Retire dead and reproducible material before introducing the final directory structure or rewriting the remaining documentation.
decisions.evidence: The user asked to remove useless code and files before polishing the surviving tree.

entries.name: principle-type-system-discipline
entries.reason: The planning route defines no production signatures or typed data model; implementation phases will apply this when consolidating typed code.

decisions.decision: Use module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, and locality consistently in every architectural finding.

decisions.decision: Use the deletion test to distinguish shallow pass-through modules from deep modules that concentrate knowledge.
decisions.evidence: .agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md deep versus shallow guidance

decisions.decision: Keep interfaces small, treat them as test surfaces, and reject hypothetical seams that have only one adapter.
decisions.evidence: .agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md principles

decisions.decision: Prefer modules whose dependencies enter through parameters and whose observable results can be checked without internal mutation.
decisions.evidence: .agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md designing for testability section

decisions.decision: Evaluate every proposed seam by the module interface it hosts, the adapters it needs, and the locality and leverage it creates.
decisions.evidence: .agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md relationships section

decisions.decision: Do not score modules by line-count ratios or confuse interfaces with language-level signatures.
decisions.evidence: .agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md rejected framings

decisions.decision: Classify dependencies before recommending that shallow modules merge or move behind a smaller interface.
decisions.evidence: .agents/skills/codebase-design/DEEPENING.md

decisions.decision: Tag each candidate dependency as in-process, local-substitutable, remote-owned, or external so its test plan is honest.
decisions.evidence: .agents/skills/codebase-design/DEEPENING.md dependency categories

decisions.decision: Keep internal test seams private and expose a new port only when production and test adapters make the seam real.
decisions.evidence: .agents/skills/codebase-design/DEEPENING.md seam discipline

decisions.decision: Replace tests of retired shallow modules with observable tests at the surviving deep module's interface.
decisions.evidence: .agents/skills/codebase-design/DEEPENING.md replace-don't-layer strategy

decisions.decision: Split the plan by independently verifiable migration phase while keeping the final repository documentation split to the fewest live branches.

decisions.decision: Use stable classification terms such as authoritative, generated, reproducible, historical, and dead throughout the plan and later manifest.

decisions.decision: Delete duplicate caches of config and commands, disclose branch-only history, and retain one source for each decision.
